summary: Parallelism holds a feature parallel to a datum. A surface or centre plane must fit between two planes parallel to the datum. An axis can use a cylinder instead.

cell.zone: A surface or centre plane must sit between two planes parallel to the datum. With a diameter symbol, an axis must sit inside a cylinder parallel to the datum.
cell.datum: Parallelism always needs a datum. The surface is held parallel to it.
cell.mmc: Parallelism can take M or L when it is put on a feature of size. On a plain surface it cannot.
cell.applies: Use it on a flat surface, or on the axis or centre plane of a feature of size.
cell.also: On a flat surface it also controls flatness, up to the same tolerance, unless the tangent plane symbol is used. It does not set the distance from the datum.
cell.confused: Shop practice: parallelism is often mixed up with flatness. Flatness has no datum. Parallelism always has one.
cell.check: Shop practice: rest the part on its datum face and sweep an indicator across the surface.
